facts.raw_span: a woman in her 60s presented with an itchy plaque on the mid-back
had had a lesion at that site since childhood, which had remained asymptomatic and pea sized for most of that time
over the 10 years prior to presentation it had gradually increased in size and became itchy
occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding from the lesion
1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
adjoining skin showed a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining
tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
several foci showed papillary projections lined by multilayered epithelium with atypical cells, few mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis but no dermal invasion
p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers
adjacent skin showed dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits
pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) immunostain positive

concepts.why: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with multiple papillary projections, vascular and plasma cell-rich stroma, and positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers supports the diagnosis of Hidradenoma Papilliferum.

The finding of a tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits suggests Eccrine Poroma, although it is less likely than Hidradenoma Papilliferum.

The presence of a tumor with multiple papillary projections and atypical cells, but no dermal invasion, could suggest Syringocystadenoma Papilliferum, although the clinical presentation is not typical.

The finding of a tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers supports the diagnosis of Apocrine Hidradenoma, although it is less likely than Hidradenoma Papilliferum.

rationales.F12: The positive pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) immunostain is consistent with Hidradenoma Papilliferum and Apocrine Hidradenoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Hidradenoma Papilliferum best explains the findings, including the circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining, papillary projections, and atypical cells without dermal invasion, along with positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers.
